reason: Driven, and the core of it holds. From owner-flight the bar reads Add a moment / Preview / Publish while the line directly beneath it reads 'Live since 15 July · anyone with the link can read it'. Pressing Publish is a same-frame swap: data-state flips to publish, document.getAnimations() returns [], there are no @keyframes in b.css or shell.css, and the only non-zero transition anywhere on the resulting page is .b-act border/background at 0.14s. Nothing is committed and no state changes, so the verb on the primary control is a lie about what the press does. What it lands on is composed for a case the artifact cannot reach: the headline is 'Send it to Mara & Finn.', the live region says 'Ready to send. The link is below.', and eighteen inches to the left the card in the same viewport says '79 days away WHEN THIS WAS SENT'. Past tense and future tense on one screen, about one event, at 1440x960. That is not taste, it is an internal contradiction, and no gate touches it: interaction-check only asserts that copy answers on the control and in a live region, that there is a way back, that the link is selectable and unbroken, and that landing says where it went. Scope is clean — protected objects are 'Nothing', DIRECTIONS.md numbers zone 3 'The publish ceremony', REFERENCE.md names 'There is no ceremony ... the moment a private plan becomes someone else's copy is a form' as a defect of the before, and lock.md lists A's press stamp on publish as an idea worth folding in if it earns it. The proposed motion is inside the ladder: 0.22s is a declared duration, cubic-bezier(0.23, 1, 0.32, 1) is the declared family, the fix says no scale and no bounce, and shell.css's blanket prefers-reduced-motion block already strips any transition added. No colour, no weight, no architecture. The taste half is argued rather than asserted — it names the mandate, names what the surface actually holds, and refuses the replay on cost grounds. Three inaccuracies, none fatal: 'THE MOMENT IT BECOMES THEIRS' is the review console's caption (CAPTIONS.publish in render-core.js), rendered on the frame but lab chrome, not the state's own kicker; the fixture does not 'already distinguish' the two cases, it hardcodes publication.state 'published' and it is render-b.js that branches ('Only you can see this'); and the empty band is ~260px of 960 below the content, not the bottom half, though with ~270px above it the composition does sit in a band across the middle of the window.
sharpenedFix: Split the fix and lead with the half that is gradeable on this artifact. (1) The label: on a plan whose own line says 'Live since 15 July', the owner bar's primary control must not say 'Publish' — branch it on F.publication.state exactly as .b-shared already does, 'Publish' when unpublished, 'Get the link' or 'Send it on' when live. (2) The destination's copy: on the live case the screen must stop pretending this is the first send. Headline the fact ('Mara & Finn have had this since 15 July.'), make Copy the link the primary act, and drop 'Ready to send. The link is below.' — it contradicts the card beside it, which already says 'when this was sent'. Keep 'Sending comes next'; keep the revoke line. (3) Only then the ceremony, and only on the unpublished branch, which today has no route in at all (owner-empty carries an inert 'Nothing to preview yet', not a Publish). It needs the count, the date and the day's name settling into the card's geometry on top/opacity at var(--t-slow) with var(--ease), no scale, no bounce, landing on one line of voice type naming who can now open it, and the .b-shared line flipping to a true 'Live since <today>'. Argue it against b.css's own motion doctrine before building it — that comment says position is animated because it renders a change of quantity, not to decorate a state change, and a composing card has to earn its way past that on the ground that this state change IS the quantity changing hands. If it cannot, ship (1) and (2), which are copy and a branch, not a build, and which remove a contradiction the panel can see at 1440x960 today.
